title: Jesus catches Peter Part 1
scripture_text: ‘’One day as Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, the people were crowding around him and listening to the word of God. He saw at the water’s edge two boats, left there by the fishermen, who were washing their nets. He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from shore. Then he sat down and taught the people from the boat. When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch.” Simon answered, “Master, we’ve worked hard all night and haven’t caught anything. But because you say so, I will let down the nets.” When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break. So they signalled their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink. When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees and said, “Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man!” For he and all his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken, and so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, Simon’s partners. Then Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid; from now on you will fish for people.’’ So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed him.’’
devotional:
The Context of this story.

Some people read this story as Jesus calling Peter to follow Him: they see it as Peter’s initial call to leave all he has and to follow him, however, I don’t think that is the case. At this time Peter had a relationship with Jesus, he knew and loved Jesus. If we were to look at the other gospels we know a number of things about Peter’s relationship with Jesus.

Peter was introduced to Jesus by his brother Andrew. John 1:41

Peter had been promised by Jesus that he would be changed and transformed by Jesus. John 1:42

Peter had some desire to follow Jesus. See Matthew 4:18-19. At this time Peter had an incomplete understanding of what it meant to follow Jesus fully.

Jesus spent time in Peter’s home, and while he was there Jesus healed Peter’s mother in law. Luke 4:38-39.

Peter’s experience of Jesus up to this point was wonderful, but it wasn’t sufficient to sustain a lifelong whole hearted devotion to Jesus. Peter’s thinking and perspective on life were completely reoriented by an experience of the holiness of Jesus. This was a ‘light bulb’ moment in Peter’s life. So as Peter began to haul in that huge catch of fish, a lot of lights went on, and Peter’s world was never the same. It was an experience that brought clarification and deep understanding. As Peter was struggling with this huge catch of fish, he was in the process of grasping truths that he up to now was unable to grasp. Sometimes the purpose of the blessings of God is to expose our sin.

Before we look at how this revelation affected Peter, let me just mention how it came about. Without retelling the story I just want us to notice two ways in which Jesus prepared Peter’s heart for a deeper understanding of him.

Jesus invaded Peter’s space.

We are told by Luke that ‘’Jesus ‘saw two boats left there by the fishermen. He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon. He asked Simon to put out a little from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the people from the boat.’’ Five times in the story Luke refers to the boats, and his last reference mentions that the boats were beginning to sink. Why so much emphasis on the boats?

The boat was a symbol of Peter’s identity, livelihood and significance. Jesus had been in Peter’s house, Luke 4:38. But now Jesus was going to invade Peter’s personal space. Peter’s boat was where he was in charge, where he was in control. It was where he could be himself, where he knew what to do and how to do it. His boat was his badge of competence, his sphere of proficiency, a representation of his expertise. Getting into Peter’s boat was Jesus’ way of getting to the very heart Peter.

The second thing that Jesus did, was to teach Peter that his work in Peter’s life could not be confined or defined by Peter’s understanding or experience. Everything that Jesus asked Peter to do was contrary to all Peter’s training, understanding and experience as a professional fisherman. To go out onto the lake in the middle of the day with the hope of catching fish was a waste of time and energy. However, Peter was going to learn that Jesus has the ability and the right to work outside the normal confines of the conventional. Neither Jesus nor his dealings with us can be boxed, neatly packaged or conveniently pigeon-holed, by the limitations of our understanding or experience.

As the tons of fish began to enter Peter’s nets, it dawned on Peter that Jesus had not only the power to heal people and exorcise demons, but he had control over the whole of creation, even the allusive fish that Peter and his friends were unable to net the previous night. In verse 8 Peter refers to Jesus as Lord which means authoritative ownership. His evaluation and understanding of who Jesus was underwent a substantial change from master to Lord. In doing so he was giving him the supreme place in his life; he was pledging him implicit obedience and reverent worship.
prayer: Father may I know Jesus as my Lord.
